behavior: Forages by hitching upward in short, jerky spirals around trunks and large branches, bracing with its stiff tail and probing bark crevices for insects and spiders; usually flies down to the base of another tree to begin again.
field_marks: Slim, bark-clinging body with mottled brown-and-buff upperparts
Broad buff eyebrow above a dark eye line
Dark wings with buff spotting and a pale wing bar
Long, stiff, pointed tail; short legs with strongly curved claws
habitat: Primarily mature coniferous, deciduous, and mixed forests with large trees for foraging and loose-barked dead or dying trees for nesting; uses a wider variety of wooded habitats outside the breeding season.
